assumptions: n >= 3, kappa >= 4, and O is real orthogonal. There are no further hypotheses, including no special-orthogonal restriction.
conclusion: The scalar identity det(O) sqrt(det(Q)) = (1/(2^n)) det(B) holds, with the signed determinant det(O) retained.
constant_dependencies: No existential or unspecified constants occur. All numerical coefficients are fixed as displayed. Matrix dimension and the identity depend on n; Q and the displayed auxiliary matrix depend on n, kappa, and O. Where present, 1/(2^n) depends only on n. The square root of kappa depends only on kappa.
domains: n is a natural number; kappa is real; O and I are real n by n matrices indexed by Fin n. O belongs to the full real orthogonal group O(n), with no determinant +1 restriction. Scalar coefficients, determinants, and square roots are real.
objects: A real orthogonal matrix O, the identity matrix I, Q = ((kappa + 1)/2) I - ((kappa - 1)/4)(O + O^T), B = (sqrt(kappa) + 1) O - (sqrt(kappa) - 1) I, and their real determinants and scalar square roots.
quantifiers: Universally quantify n, then impose n >= 3; universally quantify kappa, then impose kappa >= 4; universally quantify every O in the real orthogonal group of dimension n.
reconstructed_theorem_text: For every natural number n with n >= 3, every real number kappa with kappa >= 4, and every real orthogonal n by n matrix O, let I be the n by n identity matrix and let Q = ((kappa + 1)/2) I - ((kappa - 1)/4)(O + O^T). Then det(O) sqrt(det(Q)) = 2^(-n) det((sqrt(kappa) + 1) O - (sqrt(kappa) - 1) I). Both square roots are nonnegative real square roots. The assertion holds for the full orthogonal group, including matrices of determinant -1, and retains the factor det(O) on the left.
scopes: The outer square root applies to the scalar determinant of the entire matrix Q, and det(O) multiplies that root. In B the square root applies only to kappa. The factor 1/(2^n) multiplies the determinant of the entire matrix B. The equality is scalar and includes both determinant components of O(n).
